thread.title: Dow Stocks Drop 4.4% in a Turkey of a Week

title: Dow Stocks Drop 4.4% in a Turkey of a Week
text:

https://www.barrons.com/articles/dow-stocks-drop-4-4-in-a-turkey-of-a-week-1543022308 Dow Stocks Drop 4.4% in a Turkey of a Week By Nov. 23, 2018 8:18 p.m. ET Order Reprints Photograph by Sharon McCutcheon Text size
Stocks had one of their worst weeks of the year as the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1,127 points, or 4.4%, to 24,285, its lowest closing level since July.
The blue-chip index was depressed by concerns about the economic outlook and particular weakness in three components: Apple (ticker: AAPL), which dropped nearly 11% to $172.29; Boeing (BA), which was off 6.7% to $312.32; and Goldman Sachs Group (GS), which fell 6.4% to $189.10.
The S&P 500 declined 104 points, or 3.8%, to 2632, and the Nasdaq Composite was off 308 points, or 4.3%, to 6939. The Dow is off 1.8% so far this year, while the S&P 500 has fallen 1.5%. The Nasdaq is one of the few U.S. indexes still in the black for 2018, with a gain of 0.5%.
Oil prices continued their recent plunge, with West Texas Intermediate crude dropping 7.8% Friday, to $50.39 a barrel. It’s now off 34% from its October high of $76. Friday’s sharp drop—which didn’t appear to reflect any specific news in energy markets—prompted a 3% fall in energy stocks, as measured by the Energy Select Sector SPDR exchange-traded fund (XLE). It finished the week at a new 52-week low and is off almost 10% in 2018.
“There is some speculation that oil demand is slowing, but there hasn’t been any definitive data to support a supply/demand imbalance that would lead to this kind of a downdraft in the stocks,” says Mark Stoeckle, a portfolio manager at Adams Funds. His firm’s Adams Natural Resources closed-end fund (PEO) fell 8%, to $16 last week, a roughly 16% discount to its net asset value. It yields over 4%. He favors EOG Resources (EOG) and Occidental Petroleum (OXY).
The oil markets are on edge ahead of an important OPEC meeting on Dec. 6 amid ongoing speculation about what Saudi Arabia may do to try to lift oil prices.
The major U.S. integrated oil companies, Exxon Mobil (XOM) and Chevron (CVX), both dropped 4% last week, with Exxon finishing at $75.49 and Chevron at $113.60. They both yield around 4%. European super-major Royal Dutch Shell (RDS.A) was off about 5% to $59, a new 52-week low, and now yields over 6% (before U.S. withholding taxes). Most of the major energy companies are seen as capable of covering their dividends from free cash flow as long as Brent crude, now at $59, holds above $50.
Stocks could find support because the S&P 500 now trades at its lowest valuation since the market drop in early 2016, Bloomberg data show. The index is valued at 16 times this year’s expected operating earnings of about $163 and less than 15 times projected 2019 earnings of $178. Investors are fearful that 2019 earnings estimates won’t pan out because of potential global economic weakness, but some reduction in growth already seems discounted in the market.
Another potential bullish development for stocks is that investors are scaling back their expectations about the extent of further interest-rate increases by the Federal Reserve. The market now discounts a quarter-point boost in a key short rate, currently in the 2%-2.25% range, in December and possibly just one more in 2019, compared with the recent expectations among members of the policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee of three quarter-point moves. More in Trader Corporate America Is Ready to Pay Down Its Debt. That’s Bad News for Stocks.
Battered home-building stocks may be starting to discount Fed restraint, as the group has been strong lately despite generally weaker sales and traffic data. Toll Brothers (TOL) gained 7% last week, to $32.60, D.R. Horton (DHI) was up 3%, to $35.81, and Lennar (LEN) gained 4%, to $42.74. Investors are gravitating to the stocks because valuations are low and mortgage rates could be heading lower next year. Toll and Lennar trade around book value, and the major builders remain highly profitable, with P/Es in the seven to eight range—one of the lowest valuations of any industry.
Wall Street will be focused on President Donald Trump’s meeting with President Xi Jinping of China at this week’s G-20 meeting in Argentina, where the two leaders are expected to discuss trade issues.
In a conciliatory move, Chinese antitrust regulators on Friday cleared United Technologies ’ (UTX) $23 billion purchase of Rockwell Collins (COL). The approval, the last remaining hurdle to the deal, led to a 9% gain in Rockwell shares Friday, to $141.63. The deal had been viewed as hostage to U.S.-China trade tensions, with investors effectively giving it just a 50% chance of approval. United Technologies, which expects to close the transaction in the coming week, rose 2.7% Friday to $129.04.
